Apple officially confirmed yesterday that it will hold a product launch event next week (October 13). The event, themed "Welcome Home" (歡迎回家), is expected to focus on new smart home products. Below is everything anticipated at Apple's launch event next week.

9to5Mac's Apple launch event coverage is sponsored by Sony: Sony is running a major sale on Amazon, with significant discounts across its entire range of televisions, including models that support Apple AirPlay 2.

Apple「歡迎回家」event details

As Ryan mentioned, this event is split into two parts: an in-person experience for the media in New York City, and what Mark Gurman described as an "online video release."

This means we can expect press releases and videos (or multiple videos) to go out around 9 AM Eastern Time (6 AM Pacific Time) on October 13. Apple has not confirmed this arrangement, so the actual release time may change. But at the very least, we know Apple will announce something on October 13 — some people can attend in person, while the rest of us will be watching from home.

What to expect

The "HomePad" smart display

The highlight next week is Apple's long-rumored smart display product, which we have been calling the "HomePad." Apple sees this product as potentially becoming the hub of the home, powered by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

According to Bloomberg, the device will feature a 6-inch square display mounted on a hemispherical base, supported by a metal arm. Reports say the HomePad will come in two versions: one that can be mounted on a wall, and one that sits on a tabletop. The design is described as being similar to Apple's classic iMac G4.

One of the HomePad's standout features is the ability to recognize different people in the household. According to Mark Gurman, it can identify who is speaking to it or approaching it, and dynamically adjust what is shown on screen.

On the software side, reports suggest the HomePad will blend elements from the Apple Watch, Apple TV, and iPad — including an iPad-like app design, Apple Watch-style icons, and heavy inspiration from the iPhone's widgets and StandBy mode.

The new Apple TV 4K

Apple is also expected to unveil a new Apple TV 4K next week — the first update to the set-top box since November 2022. The new Apple TV will look the same as the previous generation, but is reportedly set to feature an A19 or A19 Pro chip.

With the chip upgrade, Apple will be able to bring Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features to the Apple TV for the first time.

Apple is reportedly developing new software features for both the Apple TV and HomePod. For example, code references point to a new feature that would allow four full-size HomePods to be paired with an Apple TV to create a surround sound system.

HomePod mini 2

The HomePod mini will also receive its first major upgrade next week. The biggest change is a new chip that is significantly faster than the S5 processor in the current model, and supports Siri AI. For some background, the S5 chip used in the current HomePod mini is the same one Apple first introduced in the Apple Watch Series 5.

In addition to the faster chip, the new HomePod mini 2 is reportedly set to come in new colours:

  • Pink
  • White
  • Green
  • Blue
  • Black

Easter egg: new "second-party" smart home accessories

Finally, Apple is working with LG to develop new "second-party" accessories for HomeKit. Products reportedly being co-developed by Apple and LG include smart door locks, thermostats, doorbells, and a range of cameras.

Bloomberg says Apple is "at least several months away" from releasing these accessories. However, they may still make an appearance next week as part of Apple's overall smart home strategy.

  • Apple's new Home "second-party" accessories are bigger than expected (leak)
  • Leaked images reveal Apple's new Home smart door lock, thermostat, and more developed for LG
  • Leaked images give the first look at new Home cameras and doorbells from Apple and LG's collaboration
  • Apple's new HomeKit "second-party" products will get exclusive iPhone feature

Wrap-up

Even with all these rumours, I have a fairly clear picture of what Apple will announce next week, but I'm still really looking forward to seeing the company officially lay out its smart home roadmap. It feels like Apple has neglected this area for too long — hopefully, next week, Apple will finally take it seriously.

What are you most looking forward to seeing at Apple's "Welcome Home" event next week? Are you planning to pick up a new HomePad, or upgrade your Apple TV and HomePod mini? Let us know in the comments.
